\subsection{Analytical primary codebook}

Sample scale and Cartesian levels are
\begin{equation}
 \sigma^2=\frac{1}{n_t d}\sum_{i=0}^{n_t-1}\|x_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad D_s=d/M,\qquad K=2^B.
 \label{eq:4-scale}
\end{equation}
\[
 B=D_s=8\Longrightarrow
 \mathcal C_m=\{-a,+a\}^{8},\quad a=0.674\sigma.
\]
Eight signs fit a byte, enabling $O(d)$ encoding/split LUTs \cite{jhq} (\cref{sec:5-2}). Arbitrary Lloyd updates may break Cartesian structure.

For fixed sign vector $s\in\{-1,+1\}^d$,
\begin{equation}
 \|q'-a s\|^2=\|q'\|^2+da^2-2a\langle q',s\rangle.
 \label{eq:4-sign-ranking}
\end{equation}
\[
 a>0\Longrightarrow
 \arg\min_s\|q'-as\|^2=\arg\max_s\langle q',s\rangle.
\]
The order needs $a>0$, not Gaussian data. Residuals depend on $a$; zero scale/FP32 ties are separate cases.



\subsection{Coarse assignment as filter and refine}

IVF initialises spaced rotated rows and runs eight iterations using $s_\ell=\|\mu_\ell\|^2-2\langle y,\mu_\ell\rangle$. Supported dimensions use int8 filtering, resolving ambiguity in FP32.

\begin{resultblock}
\begin{lemma}[Assignment with certified score intervals]
\label{lem:4-assignment-bound}
Let $\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell$ be dequantised approximations,
$e=y-\widetilde y$ and $f_\ell=\mu_\ell-\widetilde\mu_\ell$.
Keeping centroid norms exact, the approximate score
$\widetilde s_\ell=\|\mu_\ell\|^2-2\langle\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle$
has real-arithmetic error bounded by
\begin{equation}
 E_\ell=2\bigl(\|y\|\|f_\ell\|+\|e\|\|\widetilde\mu_\ell\|\bigr).
 \label{eq:4-assignment-bound}
\end{equation}
Given valid intervals $[L_\ell,U_\ell]$ containing every target score,
discarding only $L_\ell>\min_j U_j$ and exactly resolving the remaining
scores preserves the minimum and its specified tie rule.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Using $e=y-\widetilde y$ and $f_\ell=\mu_\ell-\widetilde\mu_\ell$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle y,\mu_\ell\rangle-
 \langle\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle
 &=\langle y,f_\ell\rangle
   +\langle e,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle,\\
 |s_\ell-\widetilde s_\ell|
 &\leq2\bigl(\|y\|\|f_\ell\|
       +\|e\|\|\widetilde\mu_\ell\|\bigr)=E_\ell .
 \end{aligned}
\]
For $j^*\in\arg\min_j U_j$,
\[
 L_\ell>U_{j^*}
 \Longrightarrow
 s_\ell\geq L_\ell>U_{j^*}\geq s_{j^*}.
\]
The strict inequality excludes $\ell$; equality stays eligible.
\end{proof}
\end{resultblock}

The FP32 safety margin does not prove identical assignments without a
bound on accumulation error. FP16 differs on 0/14,838 Vogue, 6/31,748 BGE and 3/16,359 Stella tail assignments. Cold logs do not identify precision.

\subsection{Residual fitting and the iteration budget}

Residuals stay $r=\Pi x-\widehat p(x)$. Per subspace, GPU sorting/Lloyd fits $K_r=2^{B_r}$ sorted scalar levels shared across coordinates, capped at 2,000 updates.

Historical 100K training gained 0.0063--0.0076 recall at 25$\to$2,000 updates. Tail-bin/BGE/Stella changes persisted: the cap is not convergence, without contradicting exact Lloyd descent. At 20,000 updates, historical Stella all-row/100K recall was 0.9921/0.9920.

\subsection{Construction work and observed imbalance}

\[
 W_{\rm QR}=O(d^3),\qquad W_{\rm rotate}=O(n_t d^2).
\]
Direct coarse assignment costs $O(n_t n_{\rm list}d)$ per iteration.
\[
 W_{\rm primary}=O(MKD_s),\qquad
 W_{\rm residual\ extraction}=O(n_rd),
\]
followed by sorting and scalar updates. These describe work, rather than predict latency.
Synchronised phase diagnostics place about 83\% of BGE/Stella training
in IVF k-means (about 2.97\,s). They use one add buffer and forced
synchronisation, separately from the normal overlapped timings in
\cref{sec:7-7}.


List-size imbalance enters the scan rule in \cref{sec:5-5}. The
individual contributions of eight IVF iterations, spaced seeds and
finite sampling to that imbalance were not isolated.


\paragraph{Arithmetic used in the measured implementation.}
The evaluated implementation (v69) stores FP32 matrices but enables cuBLAS
TF32 tensor-core math for $d\geq1{,}536$. This affects
training/add/query rotation and centroid GEMMs on both OpenAI datasets;
the implementation's environment switch cannot disable this mode. Thus FP32 storage does
not imply full FP32 multiplication. The supplementary FP32 variant (v72)
corrects this switch. Its sensitivity experiment reuses the same
TF32-trained cache and changes add/query arithmetic, rather than retraining
the model in FP32 (\cref{sec:7-precision}).

\subsection{Codebook structure and lookup cost}

Mailman, a method that reuses sums for codes with finitely many coordinate
values, gains no
speed here; two-group LUTs usually win (\cref{fig:7-lut}). Codebook quality must therefore be evaluated with achievable table placement/access cost (\cref{sec:5-2,sec:5-3}).

\subsection{Parallelism and selection overhead}

Once queries supply enough parallelism, staging/selection/merge overhead can dominate (\cref{fig:7-batch}). The Vogue and BGE results suggest also considering candidate counts
and partition/merge costs when scheduling (\cref{sec:7-2,sec:7-6}). Richer scheduling must repay calibration; bounds alone are not isolated.

\subsection{Refinement speed and budget savings}

Assume fixed $T_0>0$, refinement times $F_h\geq F_\ell>0$ and common multiplier $\eta\in(0,1]$. The low-budget speedup and
its derivatives are
\begin{align}
 S(\eta,T_0)&=\frac{T_0+\eta F_h}{T_0+\eta F_\ell},
 \label{eq:8-refinement-sensitivity}\\
 \frac{\partial S}{\partial\eta}
 &=\frac{T_0(F_h-F_\ell)}{(T_0+\eta F_\ell)^2}\geq0,\qquad
 \frac{\partial S}{\partial T_0}
 =\frac{\eta(F_\ell-F_h)}{(T_0+\eta F_\ell)^2}\leq0.\nonumber
\end{align}
For $F_h>F_\ell$, faster refinement reduces the value of cutting its
budget; lower fixed cost increases it. The derivatives hold with
non-refinement work fixed. Budget-dependent scan maintenance and
resource transitions require the controlled comparisons of
\cref{sec:7-5,sec:7-stream-cost}. Quality and reuse remain constraints
(\cref{tab:7-budget-full,fig:7-budget-risk}).

The initial JHQ refinement multipliers are 64, 100, 8 and 4 for
Vogue/arXiv/OpenAI-1536/OpenAI-3072; coverage extensions remain in the
records. For measured points $a,b$, let $R$ be recall and $Q$ throughput.
A point is dominated if another has no lower recall or throughput and
improves at least one:
\[
 a\succ b\iff R_a\geq R_b,\ Q_a\geq Q_b,\
 (R_a,Q_a)\ne(R_b,Q_b).
\]
For target recall $r$, the qualifying measured throughput is
\begin{equation}
Q_{\rm meas}(r)=\max\{Q_i:R_i\geq r\}.
\label{eq:3-measured-frontier}
\end{equation}
Without a qualifying point, this value is undefined. Between adjacent
frontier points bracketing the target, log-throughput interpolation gives
\begin{equation}
\log Q_{\rm int}(r)=(1-\lambda)\log Q_a+\lambda\log Q_b,
\qquad \lambda=\frac{r-R_a}{R_b-R_a}.
\label{eq:3-interpolated-frontier}
\end{equation}

查询通过页锁定（pinned）暂存缓冲上传，即使用不会被操作系统换页的主机内存进行 GPU 传输。JHQ 输出使用普通可换页（pageable）主机内存，基线输出使用页锁定内存。JHQ／RaBitQ 程序使用 C++，CAGRA／IVF-PQ 使用 Python。接口成本计入测量，对小 batch 与接近持平的比较尤其重要。

对大小为 $b$ 的 batch，第 $r$ 轮包含 $m_r$ 次调用，每次耗时 $t_{ri}$，单位为秒。先用轮内平均调用时间计算吞吐，再取各轮吞吐的中位数：
\begin{equation}
 \bar t_r=\frac1{m_r}\sum_{i=1}^{m_r}t_{ri},
 \qquad Q_r=\frac b{\bar t_r},
 \qquad Q=\operatorname{median}_r Q_r.
 \label{eq:3-throughput}
\end{equation}
E1 使用大小为 1,000 的 batch，测量五轮，通常每轮 24 次。JHQ 每个变体／轮次预热一次；基线起初预热三次，并为慢配置减少计时调用数。驱动即时（just-in-time，JIT）编译和 CUDA Graph 捕获均在计时前完成；后者记录 GPU 操作，供后续重复执行。调用时间分位数描述同步 batch，而非并发请求的尾延迟。

有效的慢调用保留在均值中。以示意时间 $(1,1,10)$\,ms 为例，
\[
 \bar t=4\,\mathrm{ms}\ne\operatorname{median}(t)=1\,\mathrm{ms},
 \qquad b/\bar t\ne b/\operatorname{median}(t).
\]
重复计时轮次共享同一索引；独立训练波动需要单独冷建库测量。

E1 使用 RTX 5090，显存 32,607\,MiB，驱动 595.71.05，CUDA 13.0，cuVS 26.08.01，功率上限 575\,W。OpenMP 使用 16 个线程，环境提供 25 个逻辑 CPU。JHQ 编译目标：compute\_80 PTX，由驱动即时编译 \cite{cuda_platform}。GPU 时钟和主机后台活动未受控制，可能带来计时波动；吞吐量由五轮测量汇总得到。

显存统计区分索引分配、搜索时进程分配与构建峰值。进程总占用包含上下文和工作区；JHQ 的净值扣除背景分配，CAGRA 的索引增量则衡量索引分配（\cref{sec:4-4,sec:7-7}），二者边界不同。构建峰值每 20\,ms 采样，可能遗漏更短的瞬时峰值；构建时间覆盖 train／add 调用，不含输入载入。

\subsection{Transform and sampling}

QR factorisation on the host splits a seeded Gaussian matrix into
orthogonal and upper-triangular factors; the orthogonal factor gives
square $\Pi$:
\begin{equation}
 Y_t=X_t\Pi^{\mathsf T},\qquad y=\Pi x,\qquad
 \|\Pi(q-x)\|_2^2=\|q-x\|_2^2
 \quad\text{when }\Pi^{\mathsf T}\Pi=I.
 \label{eq:4-transform}
\end{equation}
The geometry contract (K0) checks rounding in QR and general matrix
multiplication (GEMM);
dimension remains $d$ (\cref{sec:4-6}).

Primary/IVF training selects regularly spaced database rows, requesting
$n_t=39n_{\rm list}$:
\[
 n_t=\begin{cases}159{,}744,&\text{Vogue},\\319{,}488,&\text{arXiv/OpenAI},\\1{,}277{,}952,&\text{BGE/Stella}.\end{cases}
\]
This is Faiss's warning threshold, not a quality guarantee \cite{faiss_clustering}. Residual fitting uses 100,000 rows.

An older twelve-cell Vogue/OpenAI-3072 sweep ($B_r=4/8$, probes 32/128/256) fixed primary/IVF models. With 25 Lloyd iterations, 100K rather than all rows lost at most 0.0018 recall (eleven losses/one tie). Intermediate sizes were non-monotone; this supports bounded training only within that protocol.

\subsection{Analytical primary codebook}

Sample scale and Cartesian levels are
\begin{equation}
 \sigma^2=\frac{1}{n_t d}\sum_{i=0}^{n_t-1}\|x_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad D_s=d/M,\qquad K=2^B.
 \label{eq:4-scale}
\end{equation}
\[
 B=D_s=8\Longrightarrow
 \mathcal C_m=\{-a,+a\}^{8},\quad a=0.674\sigma.
\]
Eight signs fit a byte, enabling $O(d)$ encoding/split LUTs \cite{jhq} (\cref{sec:5-2}). Arbitrary Lloyd updates may break Cartesian structure.

For fixed sign vector $s\in\{-1,+1\}^d$,
\begin{equation}
 \|q'-a s\|^2=\|q'\|^2+da^2-2a\langle q',s\rangle.
 \label{eq:4-sign-ranking}
\end{equation}
\[
 a>0\Longrightarrow
 \arg\min_s\|q'-as\|^2=\arg\max_s\langle q',s\rangle.
\]
The order needs $a>0$, not Gaussian data. Residuals depend on $a$; zero scale/FP32 ties are separate cases.



\subsection{Coarse assignment as filter and refine}

IVF initialises spaced rotated rows and runs eight iterations using $s_\ell=\|\mu_\ell\|^2-2\langle y,\mu_\ell\rangle$. Supported dimensions use int8 filtering, resolving ambiguity in FP32.

\begin{resultblock}
\begin{lemma}[Assignment with certified score intervals]
\label{lem:4-assignment-bound}
Let $\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell$ be dequantised approximations,
$e=y-\widetilde y$ and $f_\ell=\mu_\ell-\widetilde\mu_\ell$.
Keeping centroid norms exact, the approximate score
$\widetilde s_\ell=\|\mu_\ell\|^2-2\langle\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle$
has real-arithmetic error bounded by
\begin{equation}
 E_\ell=2\bigl(\|y\|\|f_\ell\|+\|e\|\|\widetilde\mu_\ell\|\bigr).
 \label{eq:4-assignment-bound}
\end{equation}
Given valid intervals $[L_\ell,U_\ell]$ containing every target score,
discarding only $L_\ell>\min_j U_j$ and exactly resolving the remaining
scores preserves the minimum and its specified tie rule.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Using $e=y-\widetilde y$ and $f_\ell=\mu_\ell-\widetilde\mu_\ell$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle y,\mu_\ell\rangle-
 \langle\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle
 &=\langle y,f_\ell\rangle
   +\langle e,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle,\\
 |s_\ell-\widetilde s_\ell|
 &\leq2\bigl(\|y\|\|f_\ell\|
       +\|e\|\|\widetilde\mu_\ell\|\bigr)=E_\ell .
 \end{aligned}
\]
For $j^*\in\arg\min_j U_j$,
\[
 L_\ell>U_{j^*}
 \Longrightarrow
 s_\ell\geq L_\ell>U_{j^*}\geq s_{j^*}.
\]
The strict inequality excludes $\ell$; equality stays eligible.
\end{proof}
\end{resultblock}

The FP32 safety margin does not prove identical assignments without a
bound on accumulation error. FP16 differs on 0/14,838 Vogue, 6/31,748 BGE and 3/16,359 Stella tail assignments. Cold logs do not identify precision.

\subsection{Residual fitting and the iteration budget}

Residuals stay $r=\Pi x-\widehat p(x)$. Per subspace, GPU sorting/Lloyd fits $K_r=2^{B_r}$ sorted scalar levels shared across coordinates, capped at 2,000 updates.

Historical 100K training gained 0.0063--0.0076 recall at 25$\to$2,000 updates. Tail-bin/BGE/Stella changes persisted: the cap is not convergence, without contradicting exact Lloyd descent. At 20,000 updates, historical Stella all-row/100K recall was 0.9921/0.9920.

\subsection{Construction work and observed imbalance}

\[
 W_{\rm QR}=O(d^3),\qquad W_{\rm rotate}=O(n_t d^2).
\]
Direct coarse assignment costs $O(n_t n_{\rm list}d)$ per iteration.
\[
 W_{\rm primary}=O(MKD_s),\qquad
 W_{\rm residual\ extraction}=O(n_rd),
\]
followed by sorting and scalar updates. These describe work, rather than predict latency.
Synchronised phase diagnostics place about 83\% of BGE/Stella training
in IVF k-means (about 2.97\,s). They use one add buffer and forced
synchronisation, separately from the normal overlapped timings in
\cref{sec:7-7}.


List-size imbalance enters the scan rule in \cref{sec:5-5}. The
individual contributions of eight IVF iterations, spaced seeds and
finite sampling to that imbalance were not isolated.


\paragraph{Arithmetic used in the measured implementation.}
The evaluated implementation (v69) stores FP32 matrices but enables cuBLAS
TF32 tensor-core math for $d\geq1{,}536$. This affects
training/add/query rotation and centroid GEMMs on both OpenAI datasets;
the implementation's environment switch cannot disable this mode. Thus FP32 storage does
not imply full FP32 multiplication. The supplementary FP32 variant (v72)
corrects this switch. Its sensitivity experiment reuses the same
TF32-trained cache and changes add/query arithmetic, rather than retraining
the model in FP32 (\cref{sec:7-precision}).

the model in FP32 (\cref{sec:7-precision}).

Primary/IVF training selects regularly spaced database rows, requesting
$n_t=39n_{\rm list}$:
\[

\]
This is Faiss's sample-count warning threshold, rather than a guarantee
of quantisation quality \cite{faiss_clustering}.

\subsection{Analytical primary codebook}

The primary codebook is generated from the sample scale. Its Cartesian
levels preserve the coordinate structure used by the encoder and lookup
tables:
\begin{equation}
 \sigma^2=\frac{1}{n_t d}\sum_{i=0}^{n_t-1}\|x_i\|_2^2,
 \qquad D_s=d/M,\qquad K=2^B.
 \label{eq:4-scale}
\end{equation}
\[
 B=D_s=8\Longrightarrow
 \mathcal C_m=\{-a,+a\}^{8},\quad a=0.674\sigma.
\]
Eight signs fit a byte, enabling $O(d)$ encoding and split LUTs
\cite{jhq} (\cref{sec:5-2}). Unconstrained Lloyd updates can break this
Cartesian structure. For fixed sign vector $s\in\{-1,+1\}^d$, the
squared distance expands as
\begin{equation}
 \|q'-a s\|^2=\|q'\|^2+da^2-2a\langle q',s\rangle.
 \label{eq:4-sign-ranking}
\end{equation}
\[
 a>0\Longrightarrow
 \arg\min_s\|q'-as\|^2=\arg\max_s\langle q',s\rangle.
\]
For $a>0$, primary ranking therefore depends on the query/sign inner
product without requiring Gaussian data. Residuals still depend on $a$;
zero scale and FP32 ties need separate handling.

\subsection{Coarse assignment as filter and refine}

IVF initialises centroids from spaced rotated rows and runs eight
iterations using $s_\ell=\|\mu_\ell\|^2-2\langle y,\mu_\ell\rangle$.
Supported dimensions use int8 scores to filter candidates, then resolve
ambiguity in FP32. The following lemma states the condition under which
interval filtering preserves the assignment.

\begin{resultblock}
\begin{lemma}[Assignment with certified score intervals]
\label{lem:4-assignment-bound}
Let $\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell$ be dequantised approximations,
$e=y-\widetilde y$ and $f_\ell=\mu_\ell-\widetilde\mu_\ell$.
Keeping centroid norms exact, the approximate score
$\widetilde s_\ell=\|\mu_\ell\|^2-2\langle\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle$
has real-arithmetic error bounded by
\begin{equation}
 E_\ell=2\bigl(\|y\|\|f_\ell\|+\|e\|\|\widetilde\mu_\ell\|\bigr).
 \label{eq:4-assignment-bound}
\end{equation}
Given valid intervals $[L_\ell,U_\ell]$ containing every target score,
discarding only $L_\ell>\min_j U_j$ and exactly resolving the remaining
scores preserves the minimum and its specified tie rule.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Using $e=y-\widetilde y$ and $f_\ell=\mu_\ell-\widetilde\mu_\ell$,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \langle y,\mu_\ell\rangle-
 \langle\widetilde y,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle
 &=\langle y,f_\ell\rangle
   +\langle e,\widetilde\mu_\ell\rangle,\\
 |s_\ell-\widetilde s_\ell|
 &\leq2\bigl(\|y\|\|f_\ell\|
       +\|e\|\|\widetilde\mu_\ell\|\bigr)=E_\ell .
 \end{aligned}
\]
For $j^*\in\arg\min_j U_j$,
\[
 L_\ell>U_{j^*}
 \Longrightarrow
 s_\ell\geq L_\ell>U_{j^*}\geq s_{j^*}.
\]
The strict inequality excludes $\ell$; equality stays eligible.
\end{proof}
\end{resultblock}

Valid score intervals are essential: an FP32 safety margin without an
accumulation-error bound does not certify identical assignments. Archived
FP16 tail-assignment comparisons report differences on 0/14,838 Vogue,
6/31,748 BGE and 3/16,359 Stella assignments. Cold-build logs do not
identify the assignment precision used.

\subsection{Residual fitting and the iteration budget}

Residuals are defined relative to the primary reconstruction,
$r=\Pi x-\widehat p(x)$. Residual fitting uses 100,000 rows. Within each
subspace, GPU sorting and Lloyd updates fit $K_r=2^{B_r}$ sorted scalar
levels shared across coordinates, with a cap of 2,000 updates.

An older twelve-cell Vogue/OpenAI-3072 sweep ($B_r=4/8$, probes 32/128/256)
held the primary/IVF models fixed. At 25 Lloyd iterations, using 100K
rather than all rows lost at most 0.0018 recall (eleven losses/one tie).
Intermediate sample sizes were non-monotone, so this evidence supports
bounded residual training within that protocol.

Increasing historical 100K training from 25$\to$2,000 updates gained
0.0063--0.0076 recall. Tail-bin updates and BGE/Stella results continued
to change: reaching the cap does not establish convergence or contradict
exact Lloyd descent. At 20,000 updates, historical Stella all-row/100K
recall was 0.9921/0.9920.

\subsection{Training work and list imbalance}

The training-work model separates transform generation, sample rotation,
primary-codebook generation and residual extraction. If $n_r$ denotes
the residual-training row count, the transform terms are
\[
 W_{\rm QR}=O(d^3),\qquad W_{\rm rotate}=O(n_t d^2).
\]
Direct coarse assignment costs $O(n_t n_{\rm list}d)$ per iteration;
the remaining terms are
\[
 W_{\rm primary}=O(MKD_s),\qquad
 W_{\rm residual\ extraction}=O(n_rd),
\]
followed by sorting and scalar updates. These are operation counts.
Synchronised diagnostics place about 83\% of BGE/Stella training in IVF
k-means (about 2.97\,s). They use one add buffer and forced
synchronisation, separately from the normal overlapped measurements in
\cref{sec:7-7}. Unequal list lengths affect subsequent scan work and
motivate \cref{sec:5-5}; the effects of eight IVF iterations, spaced seeds
and finite sampling on that imbalance were not measured separately.
